source_name: ESO Logs reviewed Lokkestiiz successful-clear corpus

sample.selection: successful Lokkestiiz kills with all three reviewed Aerial Onslaught windows resolved

reviewed_conclusions.statement: Across the reviewed successful-clear corpus, Aerial Onslaught Flight 1 was consistently lighter than Flights 2 and 3 in combined incoming pressure and healer output demand.
Aerial Onslaught Flight 2 was the highest combined incoming-pressure window in 9 of 10 reviewed successful kills and also required the highest healer output in 9 of 10.
Aerial Onslaught Flight 3 had player deaths in 4 of 10 reviewed successful kills, the highest death-window incidence of the three flights in this corpus.
Flights 2 and 3 each contained player interrupt activity in 9 of 10 reviewed successful kills, compared with 4 of 10 for Flight 1.
All three reviewed Aerial Onslaught windows retained substantial non-boss hostile damage, supporting treatment as boss-unavailable, add-active combat rather than global raid downtime.

strategy_implications.guidance: Treat Aerial Onslaught as active add-combat time rather than raid downtime; boss-only uptime denominators should exclude the airborne interval without excluding the raid's ongoing combat work.
Prepare strongest sustained healing coverage for Flight 2; it was the highest-pressure and highest-healer-output flight in 9 of 10 reviewed successful kills.
Expect more execution and recovery risk in Flight 3; it showed the highest player-death incidence in the reviewed successful-clear corpus.
Preserve interrupt awareness during Flights 2 and 3; interrupt activity appeared in 9 of 10 reviewed successful kills for each later flight.

limitations: Observed timings and pressure values are corpus measurements, not universal fixed encounter constants.
The corpus contains successful clears from four ESO Logs reports and should not be treated as a population-wide performance benchmark.
Raw ESO actor and ability IDs remain evidence signatures only and are not canonical semantic identity.
Strategy implications are reviewed conclusions from repeated runtime observation and remain separate from canonical mechanics truth.
